seoTitle: How to Allow Canva Microphone & Camera Access
metaDescription: Grant Canva access to your microphone and camera in your browser or system settings so you can record voiceovers and use webcam features.
intro: Recording a voiceover or using webcam-based tools in Canva requires giving the platform permission to access your device's microphone and camera. This guide covers where to find and enable those permissions in your browser or system settings so recording features work without interruption.

steps.heading: Check your browser's site permissions
steps.body: Open your browser's settings and locate the site permissions section for Canva's domain.

steps.heading: Enable microphone access
steps.body: Find the microphone permission toggle for Canva and set it to allow access.

steps.heading: Enable camera access
steps.body: Similarly, locate the camera permission setting and switch it on for Canva.

steps.heading: Check your operating system's privacy settings
steps.body: On some devices, you may also need to grant your browser microphone and camera access at the system level.

steps.heading: Refresh and test in Canva
steps.body: Reload your Canva project and try recording a voiceover or using a camera feature to confirm access is working.

steps.heading: Troubleshoot if access is still blocked
steps.body: If recording still doesn't work, check for conflicting apps using the microphone or camera, or try a different browser.

faq.question: Why won't Canva let me record my voice?
faq.answer: This usually means microphone permissions haven't been granted in your browser or system settings for Canva's site.

faq.question: Do I need to enable permissions every time I use Canva?
faq.answer: No, once you allow microphone and camera access for Canva's domain, your browser should remember the setting for future sessions.

faq.question: Can another app block Canva from using my camera?
faq.answer: Yes, if another application is already using your camera or microphone, Canva may not be able to access it until that app releases the device.

faq.question: Does this work the same way on mobile as on desktop?
faq.answer: The general idea is the same, but the exact steps to grant permissions differ between mobile operating systems and desktop browsers.
